newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech June key M2 money +6.7 pct yr/yr without SPT.
newsitem.headline: Czech June key M2 money +6.7 pct yr/yr without SPT.

text.p: The Czech National Bank's (CNB) key money supply measure, M2, grew 6.7 percent year-on-year in June, excluding the funds from the selloff in 1995 of a stake in telephone operator SPT Telecom, a CNB statement said.
The statement added that including SPT funds, year-on-year money supply growth for June was 6.0 percent.
In May, M2 grew 6.8 percent, year-on-year, without the influence of SPT funds, and 6.1 percent including the $1.32 billion from the 1995 equity expansion and sale of a stake in SPT.

The statement said the total volume of crown and foreign currency credits in June rose 11.7 percent year-on-year, after 13.3 percent growth in May, while total crown and foreign currency deposits, which include the SPT funds, grew 6.4 percent after a 5.7 percent rise in May.
The statement said the average interest rate for new crown credits was 20.36 percent, some 120 basis points higher than in May.
CZECH M2 MONEY JUNE 1997 MAY 1997 JUNE 1996
*Includes domestic deposits connected to the $1.32 billion equity expansion of SPT Telecom a.s. in summer 1995.
The average interest rate for new credits comes after a crown crisis at the end of May forced the central bank to raise interest rates sharply and choke market liquidity.
